messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the video's camera setup to an upper-body shot from a front three-quarter angle. Change only the camera setup. Preserve the person's appearance, expression, and action, along with the existing scene. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: I'd like to change the video's camera setup to an upper-body shot from a front three-quarter angle. Change only the camera setup. Preserve the person's appearance, expression, and action, along with the existing scene. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"She stands mostly still, slowly turning her head and upper body from a three-quarter view to a full side profile.","camera":"A medium shot at eye level that remains relatively static while the subject rotates slightly.","clothing":"A form-fitting, three-quarter-sleeve dress with a colorful abstract pattern of purple, blue, yellow, and orange shapes on a dark background.","hair_color":"Black.","hairstyle":"Black hair pulled back into a high ponytail with straight, blunt bangs across the forehead.","identity":"A young woman with a slender build and light brown skin, shown from the thighs up.","scene":"An outdoor area with a stone building, metal railings, copper pipes, and a grassy hill under a clear blue sky."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output begins as a medium upper-body front three-quarter shot matching the reference framing, then remains a relatively static medium shot while the woman turns from a three-quarter view toward a side profile. The dress pattern, hair, and general outdoor setting are broadly retained, but the background and framing differ from the source's side-view walking sequence.
arguments.requested_change: Change only the camera to an upper-body shot from a front three-quarter angle, using the reference for initial direction, placement, and framing while preserving the person's appearance, expression, action, scene, timing, and progression.
uncertain: Whether the head-turn timing and progression exactly match the source action.
Whether the scene is the same location viewed from a new angle or a regenerated/modified environment.
unexpected_changes: The subject's action changed from walking across the scene to standing mostly still while turning her head and upper body.
The background composition changed substantially, with a building, copper pipes, and different stone structures visible instead of the source's side-view waterfront environment.
The framing is not consistently an upper-body shot; it remains a medium shot showing the subject from roughly the thighs up.
The subject's apparent skin tone and facial rendering differ noticeably from the source.
